crossRefs.note: since he longed for you all, and was very troubled because you had heard that he was sick.
They told him all the words of Joseph, which he had said to them. When he saw the wagons which Joseph had sent to carry…
Israel said, “It is enough. Joseph my son is still alive. I will go and see him before I die.”
Joseph prepared his chariot, and went up to meet Israel, his father, in Goshen. He presented himself to him, and fell…
Israel said to Joseph, “Now let me die, since I have seen your face, that you are still alive.”
Israel said to Joseph, “I didn’t think I would see your face, and behold, God has let me see your offspring also.”
Therefore you now have sorrow, but I will see you again, and your heart will rejoice, and no one will take your joy…
sorrowing most of all because of the word which he had spoken, that they should see his face no more. Then they…
longing to see you, remembering your tears, that I may be filled with joy;
For indeed he was sick, nearly to death, but God had mercy on him, and not on him only, but on me also, that I might…
And I wrote this very thing to you, so that, when I came, I wouldn’t have sorrow from them of whom I ought to rejoice…
that which we have seen and heard we declare to you, that you also may have fellowship with us. Yes, and our fellowship…
And we write these things to you, that our joy may be fulfilled.

translations.web: I have sent him therefore the more diligently, that when you see him again, you may rejoice, and that I may be the less sorrowful.
translations.bsb: Therefore I am all the more eager to send him, so that when you see him again you may rejoice, and I may be less anxious.
translations.kjv: I sent him therefore the more carefully, that, when ye see him again, ye may rejoice, and that I may be the less sorrowful.
translations.asv: I have sent him therefore the more diligently, that, when ye see him again, ye may rejoice, and that I may be the less sorrowful.
